def add_tag(tag: str, tags: list[str] | None = None, *, uppercase: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    result = list(tags) if tags is not None else []
    result.append(tag.upper() if uppercase else tag)
    return result

assert add_tag("red", uppercase=True) == ["RED"]
assert add_tag("blue") == ["blue"]
cards.explanation: Avoid a shared mutable default while supporting a keyword-only option.

cards.code:
from typing import TypedDict

class User(TypedDict):
    name: str
    nickname: str | None

def display(user: User) -> str:
    nickname = user["nickname"]
    return nickname if nickname is not None else user["name"]

assert display({"name": "Ada", "nickname": None}) == "Ada"
cards.explanation: Describe a payload shape and handle an optional nickname explicitly.

cards.title: Async tasks and cancellation
cards.code:
import asyncio

async def main():
    started = asyncio.Event()
    closed = []
    async def worker():
        try:
            started.set()
            await asyncio.Event().wait()
        finally:
            closed.append(True)
    task = asyncio.create_task(worker())
    await started.wait()
    task.cancel()
    try:
        await task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    assert closed == [True]

asyncio.run(main())
cards.explanation: Cancel a started worker and wait for its finally cleanup.

cards.title: Read a file with pathlib

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path = Path(folder) / "greeting.txt"
    path.write_text("Hello, Ada!", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except (OSError, UnicodeError) as error:
        raise RuntimeError("cannot read greeting") from error
    assert text == "Hello, Ada!"
cards.explanation: Write and read a UTF-8 file inside a disposable directory; report I/O and decoding failures.

cards.title: Streaming file I/O
cards.code:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path = Path(folder) / "names.txt"
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        stream.write("Ada\nLin\n")
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        names = [line.strip() for line in stream if line.strip()]
    assert stream.closed
    assert names == ["Ada", "Lin"]
cards.explanation: Stream nonempty lines while keeping the file lifetime explicit; I/O errors propagate.

cards.title: Read named columns from CSV
cards.code:
import csv
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path = Path(folder) / "orders.csv"
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=["name", "quantity"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerow({"name": "tea, green", "quantity": 3})
    try:
        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            quantities = [int(row["quantity"]) for row in csv.DictReader(stream, strict=True)]
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, csv.Error, ValueError, KeyError) as error:
        raise RuntimeError("invalid orders CSV") from error
    assert quantities == [3]
cards.explanation: Read named CSV columns with proper newline handling and explicit conversion/error handling.

cards.title: Async HTTPX and cancellation
cards.code:
import asyncio
import httpx

async def main():
    started = asyncio.Event()
    closed = []
    async def respond(request):
        try:
            started.set()
            await asyncio.Event().wait()
        finally:
            closed.append(True)
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond), timeout=5.0) as client:
        task = asyncio.create_task(client.get("https://example.test/slow"))
        await started.wait()
        task.cancel()
        try:
            await task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
    assert closed == [True]

asyncio.run(main())
cards.explanation: Cancel an HTTPX 0.28.1 request after its mock handler starts and verify cleanup. The mock does not simulate socket timeouts.

cards.title: Test a FastAPI JSON request
cards.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    quantity: int = Field(gt=0)

@app.post("/items", response_model=Item, status_code=201)
def create_item(item: Item) -> Item:
    if item.name == "unavailable":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="item unavailable")
    return item

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "tea", "quantity": 2})
    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.json() == {"name": "tea", "quantity": 2}
    assert client.post("/items", json={"name": "tea", "quantity": 0}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/items", json={"name": "unavailable", "quantity": 1}).status_code == 409
cards.explanation: Create and test a JSON route, invalid body and domain conflict entirely in process. FastAPI 0.116.1/Pydantic 2.11.7/HTTPX 0.28.1; no server is started.

cards.title: Handle HTTPX timeout and status failures
cards.explanation: HTTPX 0.28.1: simulate ReadTimeout and a 503 response locally to exercise distinct failure paths. MockTransport does not enforce network timeouts; a live transport uses the configured phase limits.
